samf-junior-2002-r2-03.title: Multiply
samf-junior-2002-r2-03.body:
Number of boxes $=xy$; number of books $=xy\times z=xyz$.

**Answer: (E) $xyz$**

samf-junior-2002-r2-04.title: Divisors of 15
samf-junior-2002-r2-04.body:
$x-1$ must divide $15$, so $x-1\in\{\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\pm15\}$. The smallest value is $x-1=-15$, i.e. $x=-14$.

**Answer: (B) $-14$**

samf-junior-2002-r2-05.title: Read the graph
samf-junior-2002-r2-05.body:
On the horizontal axis find the mark labelled 15/01/02 and go straight up to the curve. The curve is at a height between the gridlines $11$ and $12$ (a little over $11.5$).

**Answer: (C) between R11 and R12**

samf-junior-2002-r2-06.title: Pigeonhole
samf-junior-2002-r2-06.body:
There are three colours, so in the worst case Bob has two T-shirts of each colour, $2\times3=6$ T-shirts, with no three of the same colour. (There are at least two of each colour, since the white ones number $28-6-5=17$.) The $7$th T-shirt must give three of one colour.

**Answer: (E) 7**

samf-junior-2002-r2-07.title: Count
samf-junior-2002-r2-07.body:
The first digit must be $2$. Each of the other $4$ digits can be $2$ or $4$ freely, giving $2^4=16$ arrangements.

**Answer: (A) 16**

samf-junior-2002-r2-08.title: Equation
samf-junior-2002-r2-08.body:
Let Petros have $3k$ and Sammy $5k$. After spending: $(3k-30):(5k-30)=1:2$, so $2(3k-30)=5k-30$, $6k-60=5k-30$, $k=30$.

Total $=8k=$ R240.

**Answer: (B) R240**

samf-junior-2002-r2-09.title: Count seats
samf-junior-2002-r2-09.body:
If there are $m$ trips and each learner goes $t$ times, the number of seats used is $8m$ (a full vehicle each time, since each trip takes $8$) $=10t$. Hence $4m=5t$, so $m$ is a multiple of $5$. The smallest is $m=5$ (with $t=4$).

This is possible: in each trip leave out a different pair of learners, e.g. trip $i$ leaves out learners $2i-1$ and $2i$. Each learner is then left out once and goes on $4$ trips.

**Answer: (D) 5**

samf-junior-2002-r2-10.title: Angle chase
samf-junior-2002-r2-10.body:
Since $AQ\parallel BC$, $\angle QAC=\angle ACB=60^\circ$ (alternate angles). In the diagram $AP$ lies on the other side of $AC$ from $Q$, so $\angle QAP=60^\circ+2x$.

Triangle $APQ$ is isosceles with $AQ=AP$, so the base angles at $P$ and $Q$ are equal: $\angle Q=\frac{180^\circ-(60^\circ+2x)}2=60^\circ-x$.

**Answer: (E) $60^\circ-x$**

samf-junior-2002-r2-11.title: Cycle of units digits
samf-junior-2002-r2-11.body:
The units digits of powers of $2$ repeat with period $4$: $2,4,8,6,2,4,8,6,\dots$. Since $2000\equiv0\pmod4$, $2^{2000}$ ends in $6$, $2^{2001}$ in $2$ and $2^{2002}$ in $4$.

$6+2+4=12$, so the units digit is $2$.

**Answer: (B) 2**

samf-junior-2002-r2-12.title: Choose two lines from $A$ and a horizontal level
samf-junior-2002-r2-12.body:
Every triangle has vertex $A$, with two of the $7$ lines through $A$ as its sides, cut off by one of the $3$ horizontal lines (the two drawn lines and the base $BC$).

Number of pairs of lines from $A$: $\binom72=21$. Number of horizontal cuts: $3$.

Total $21\times3=63$.

**Answer: (C) 63**

samf-junior-2002-r2-14.title: Surface area
samf-junior-2002-r2-14.body:
Base area $=640\div10=64\ \text{cm}^2$, so the base side is $8$ cm. Surface area $=2\times64+4\times(8\times10)=128+320=448\ \text{cm}^2$.

Cost $=448\times15\text{c}=6720\text{c}=$ R67.20.

**Answer: (B) R67.20**

samf-junior-2002-r2-15.title: Find common words
samf-junior-2002-r2-15.body:
Sentences 1 and 2 share only 'maths', and the common word is *borg*. Sentences 1 and 3 share only 'good', common word *farn*. Sentences 2 and 3 share only 'in', common word *klar*.

So *jalez* = skills, *nurf* = harmony, *darko* = gold. "Harmony gold" is *nurf darko*, i.e. *darko nurf* (only choice D contains these two words).

**Answer: (D) darko nurf**

samf-junior-2002-r2-16.title: Multiply the factors
samf-junior-2002-r2-16.body:
Income $=$ price $\times$ number sold. The new income is $0.8\times1.2=0.96$ of the old one, a decrease of $4\%$.

**Answer: (D) decreased by 4%**

samf-junior-2002-r2-17.title: Sums
samf-junior-2002-r2-17.body:
The sum of the $n$ numbers is $np$. After removing $q$ there are $n-1$ numbers with mean $p+2$:

$np-q=(n-1)(p+2)=np+2n-p-2$, so $q=p-2n+2$.

**Answer: (E) $p-2n+2$**

samf-junior-2002-r2-19.title: Three segments
samf-junior-2002-r2-19.body:
Each shaded region is a circular segment: a sector of radius $2$ and angle $60^\circ$ with the equilateral triangle on its chord (a side of $\triangle ABC$) removed.

Sector area $=\frac16\pi\cdot2^2=\frac{2\pi}3$. Equilateral triangle of side $2$ has area $\frac{\sqrt3}4\cdot4=\sqrt3$. A segment has area $\frac{2\pi}3-\sqrt3$.

Three segments: $2\pi-3\sqrt3$.

**Answer: (A) $2\pi-3\sqrt3$**

samf-junior-2002-r2-20.title: Test each suspect
samf-junior-2002-r2-20.body:
Count how many statements are true for each possible culprit; we need exactly $2$.

- Amelia broke it: Amelia true, Bongani true, Charles false, Devine true, Edwina false: $3$ true. No.
- Bongani: Amelia true, Bongani false, Charles false, Devine false, Edwina false: $1$ true. No.
- Charles: Amelia false, Bongani true, Charles false, Devine false, Edwina true: $2$ true. Yes.
- Devine: Amelia false, Bongani false, Charles false, Devine false, Edwina false: $0$ true. No.
- Edwina: Amelia true, Bongani true, Charles true, Devine true, Edwina false: $4$ true. No.

Charles broke the window.

**Answer: (C) Charles**
